name: Horni Namesti and the Old Town
tagline: Around the UNESCO plague column, baroque in every direction
description: Olomouc's upper square, holding the Holy Trinity Column, the largest baroque sculpture group in central Europe, the town hall with its socialist-realist astronomical clock, and the restaurants and cellar bars around them. The density of baroque architecture here is startling for a city this size.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the squares, the fountains and the bars all within five minutes
pros: The UNESCO column and six baroque fountains on foot
The best restaurants and cellar bars in the city
Trams from the edge of the square in all directions
cons: Old buildings without lifts or parking

name: Univerzita and Trida Svobody
tagline: The Palacky University quarter, where the students are
description: The district around the university's central faculties and the theology campus, with student housing, cheap canteens, bookshops and the bars that keep Olomouc's nightlife going. Palacky is the second oldest university in the country and its student body is unusually large relative to the city.
bestFor: Budget stays plugged into the student calendar and the bar circuit
pros: Five minutes from the main square

name: Nova Ulice
tagline: Interwar villas and blocks southwest of the centre
description: An established residential district southwest of the old town with a mix of interwar villas, apartment buildings and the university hospital, plus its own shops and tram links. It is quieter than the centre, ten minutes away on foot, and considerably better value for a proper flat.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a decent flat and a short walk into the centre
pros: Better flats for the money than the old town
Ten minutes on foot or a short tram ride in
Quiet with local shops and the hospital nearby
cons: Mixed architecture with some tired blocks
Traffic on the main radial roads

name: Morava River and Smetana Gardens
tagline: The park ring and the riverside on the eastern side
description: The band of parks that replaced the fortifications on the eastern edge of the old town, running down to the Morava river with paths, the flower garden and the exhibition grounds. Housing here backs onto green space and the centre remains a five-minute walk across the park.
bestFor: Stays that want a run along the river and the centre still on foot
pros: Park ring and the river path immediately there
Five minutes across the gardens to the square
cons: Limited housing supply directly on the park
Few shops on the park side

name: Povel and the Southern Estates
tagline: Panel estates south of the centre, cheapest in the city
description: The socialist-era housing estates built south of the old town, with supermarkets, schools, a shopping centre and frequent trams. The architecture is uniform and the rents are the lowest in Olomouc by a clear margin, which for a longer stay is exactly the trade on offer.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the city
Direct tram into the centre in ten minutes
cons: Nothing to walk to in the evening
Feels detached from the baroque city
